title: Constitutional Rights
subtitle: The Right to Protest Peacefully
content:
ARTICLE 19(1)(a) – Freedom of Speech and Expression

Every citizen has the right to:
• Express opinions
• Raise slogans
• Hold placards and banners
• Criticize the Government
• Participate in peaceful demonstrations

Restriction:
These rights are subject only to reasonable restrictions under Article 19(2).

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

ARTICLE 19(1)(b) – Right to Assemble Peacefully

Every citizen has the right to:
• Organise protests
• Participate in marches and rallies
• Hold public meetings
• Conduct peaceful sit-ins

Restriction:
The assembly must be peaceful and without arms. Restrictions may be imposed only under Article 19(3) in the interests of public order, sovereignty, and integrity of India.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

ARTICLE 19(1)(c) – Right to Form Associations

Every citizen has the right to:
• Form groups, unions, or associations
• Organise campaigns and collective action

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

ARTICLE 21 – Right to Life and Personal Liberty

Every citizen has the right to:
• Be treated with dignity
• Be protected from arbitrary detention
• Be free from excessive or unlawful use of force

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

ARTICLE 22 – Rights Upon Arrest

If arrested, you have the right to:
• Know the grounds of your arrest
• Consult and be defended by a lawyer
• Inform a family member or friend
• Be produced before a Magistrate within 24 hours

title: Police Detention
subtitle: If In Threat of Detention
content:
POLICE DUTIES DURING A PROTEST

The police must:
• Protect peaceful protesters
• Maintain public order
• Use only necessary and proportionate force
• Respect constitutional rights

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

IF YOU ARE ARRESTED

The police must:
• Inform you of the reason for your arrest
• Tell you the applicable legal provisions
• Allow you to contact a lawyer or family member
• Produce you before a Magistrate within 24 hours
• Provide medical assistance if required

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

POLICE CANNOT

The police cannot:
• Arrest you without lawful grounds
• Use excessive or disproportionate force
• Detain you for more than 24 hours without a Magistrate's order
• Deny access to a lawyer
• Force you to delete photos or videos without legal authority

title: Important BNS Sections
subtitle: BNS Rights
content:
BNS §189 – Unlawful Assembly

An assembly of five or more persons becomes unlawful only if it has a common object prohibited by law.

Note:
A peaceful protest is NOT automatically an unlawful assembly.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

BNS §190 – Member of an Unlawful Assembly

Punishment for knowingly being part of an unlawful assembly.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

BNS §191 – Rioting

Applies when an unlawful assembly uses force or violence.

Note:
Peaceful protest ≠ Rioting.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

BNS §194 – Liability of Members

Members of an unlawful assembly may be held liable for offences committed in pursuit of the assembly's common object.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

BNS §221 – Obstructing a Public Servant

Intentionally obstructing a public servant while performing lawful duties is an offence.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

BNS §285 – Obstructing a Public Way

Wrongfully blocking roads or public pathways may constitute an offence.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

BNS §324 – Mischief

Causing damage to public or private property is punishable.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

BNS §351 – Criminal Intimidation

Threatening another person with injury to cause fear is an offence.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

BNS §352 – Intentional Insult

Intentionally insulting someone with the intent to provoke a breach of peace is punishable.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

IF YOU ARE DETAINED OR ARRESTED

You should:
• Ask: "Am I under arrest?"
• Ask which BNS section you are being arrested under
• Ask which police station you are being taken to
• Contact your lawyer or family immediately
• Remain calm and do not physically resist arrest
